story: V1-70 #175: full paired head-to-head at main 65ced88 (rerun of the 5699058 run)
machine: AMD Ryzen 9 3950X (16 cores / 32 threads), 64 GB RAM, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26220, .NET SDK 10.0.402 Release; OpenEvolve 0.3.2 (411fb59) on Python 3.13 in a venv with its pyproject dependencies (openai, pyyaml, numpy, tqdm, flask, dacite) plus psutil
driver: benchmarks/external/run_overhead_head_to_head.py --repeats 9 --workers 1,2,4,8,16 --ours-n 8000 --openevolve-n 300, run through scratch/run-h2h-when-quiet.ps1, which requires three consecutive readings of peak total CPU under 20% before it starts
machine_was_quiet: yes: 16.6%, 8.8% and 9.7% peak CPU over the three consecutive pre-run checks that opened the gate (the gate had reset six times before that, over 4 minutes of waiting). Peak CPU read 40.2% in the sample taken immediately after the driver exited, while the last OpenEvolve child processes were still tearing down; that sample is after the final measurement, not during one. An earlier attempt was discarded because another session was building a solution with ~25 MSBuild workers throughout it
method: (T(2N)-T(N)) divided by the evaluations the two runs actually completed, not by N: fresh process per run, null LLM and evaluator in-process. A non-positive difference or a hang is re-measured (three attempts), never averaged in. Per-system figures are medians of the per-repeat values; the ratio is the median of the per-repeat PAIRED ratios with a 4000-draw percentile bootstrap interval, seeded 7. Which system runs first alternates by repeat parity and each row records it in ran_first, so an execution-order effect cannot hide inside the pairing.
execution_order: alternated per repeat: even repeats run AiDotNet first, odd repeats run OpenEvolve first, so neither system always pays the cold-cache cost of going first. Every row records which system ran first in that repeat (rows[].ran_first) and each summary cell reports the split (repeats_aidotnet_first / repeats_openevolve_first, 5/4 at 9 repeats)
evaluations_verified: every row carries the completed counts both systems reported (rows[].small.Evaluations and rows[].large.Evaluations); the driver refuses a cell whose completed difference falls below n/2, and OpenEvolve rows also carry Requested so dropped iterations are visible
note: A C# controller vs a Python one is expected to favour us (R12); not a headline claim.
